whys: a row held 413 million reads and passed its bound
it held the reads of thousands of task-scoped summaries made under it, each made more than once
each was first tried as sealed, found to read below HIGH, dropped, and made again as a row whose callees start the same way
library functions` summaries read some crate`s data below HIGH, which the design assumes is rare
the span that says so names the read by id, so nobody could see which crate it was
class: a fast path whose fallback redoes the work and whose precondition (library code reads only HIGH) silently stopped holding: the cost of the miss grows with the call graph, and the report of the miss names an id
prevention: the read a sealed summary names says the crate`s name and why it is below HIGH (`Witness::cause_text` beside `read_text`, and the crate`s display name for an input of a crate); a sealed crate`s summaries read nothing of a crate outside their cover, held by a test on a proc-macro crate that uses syn; and a run found below HIGH keeps what it settled for its row instead of making it again.
